reviewContext.coreQuestion: Can the earner write a USDC number that did not come from a genuine external payer (self-transfer, fabricated log, or replay)?
reviewContext.coreAnswer: YES — via block REORG. Self-transfers are correctly filtered (record-earn.mjs:79) and fabricated logs are blocked in prod (logs come only from TRUSTED_RPC getLogs pinned to the USDC address + founder to-topic). BUT the cursor advances on the un-finalized LATEST block with no confirmation/finality lag (record-earn.mjs:64,101-102): an orphaned external Transfer is counted though it never settled, and a reorged-then-reincluded Transfer is counted TWICE. Both write a USDC number that did not come from a genuine SETTLED external payer, violating THE GOAL and INV-7. Separately, the entire real getLogs parse path (from-topic slice, value decode, topics filter) is masked by the FOUNDER_LOGS_JSON seam and untested, so a bug in the self-vs-external classification itself would ship green.

evidence.description: INV-7 external-payer filter present: MY_WALLETS = [founder, automaton 0xa3cdd4, openclaw 0x9b1ee98] (lowercased), and the sum loop adds value ONLY when from is not in MY_WALLETS — a self-transfer contributes 0.
First-run init records nothing and sets cursor=now (pre-existing balance never an earning), per INV-7 spec lines 86-87.
INV-1 pin: SHARED wallets rejected (41) and positive pin to FOUNDER_WALLET_EXPECTED 0x810f (42).
Prod root is the env-independent literal '/Users/operator/.anicca-founder'; HOME/os.homedir()/FOUNDER_DIR are inside the TEST-only ternary branch (FIND-401 stays closed).
Cursor written atomically (tmp + renameSync). FIND-501 part-2 residual addressed: the new test no longer snapshots/restores the real /Users/operator/.anicca-founder baseline.

externalInflow is a pure fold over the log set (no I/O once logs are fetched); the I/O (rpc/getLogs) is isolated and FOUNDER_TEST-seam-gated, so the classification logic is in principle unit-testable — though FIND-602 shows it is not yet actually tested.
Cursor advanced BEFORE append (crash = under-count for absent-reorg case). NOTE: the finality gap in FIND-601 breaks the 'never double-count' claim for reorgs.
